items.stem: At a local maximum of a smooth function, the first derivative is:

options.text: Zero, with the function changing from increasing to decreasing
options.rationale: Correct: a stationary point has zero first derivative; a maximum turns from rising to falling.
A positive derivative means the function is still increasing.
Smooth maxima have a defined, zero derivative.
The derivative and the value are unrelated quantities.

items.explanation: Correct: a stationary point has zero first derivative; a maximum turns from rising to falling.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about the dot and cross products are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: The dot product of two vectors is a scalar
options.rationale: Correct: a dot b yields a single number.

options.text: The cross product of two 3-D vectors is a vector perpendicular to both
options.rationale: Correct: a cross b is orthogonal to a and b.

options.text: The dot product always yields a vector
options.rationale: The dot product is a scalar, not a vector.

options.text: The cross product is defined the same way in two and three dimensions
options.rationale: The cross product is specific to three dimensions.

items.explanation: Correct: a dot b yields a single number.

items.stem: An indefinite integral must include a constant of integration because:

options.text: Differentiation loses any constant term, so antiderivatives differ by a constant
options.rationale: Correct: many functions share the same derivative, differing only by a constant.

options.text: The integral is always larger than the function
Constants make the answer look more complete
options.rationale: It is mathematically required, not cosmetic.

options.text: Definite integrals also need the constant
options.rationale: Definite integrals evaluate limits and drop the constant.

items.explanation: Correct: many functions share the same derivative, differing only by a constant.
